title: Ellipsis & Substitution
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Al omitir (ellipsis) y sustituir palabras repetitivas, tu inglés suena increíblemente fluido, natural y veloz, tal como lo hablan los nativos en un entorno corporativo de alto ritmo.

parts.visual:
En C1, la eficiencia es clave. Omitimos palabras obvias para evitar la redundancia (Ellipsis). 
Ej: She can speak French, but I can't (speak French). 
Ej: They asked me to help, but I didn't want to (help). 
Ej: Some people liked the proposal; others (people) hated it.
parts.audio: In C1, efficiency is key. We omit obvious words to avoid redundancy. This is called Ellipsis. Instead of saying 'She can speak French, but I can't speak French', you just say: She can speak French, but I can't. Another example: They asked me to help, but I didn't want to. Or: Some people liked the proposal; others hated it.

parts.visual:
Sustitución (usar palabras cortas en lugar de repetir ideas largas): 
- Usar 'so' (así/eso): 
A: Will the CEO be angry? 
B: I think SO. / I hope SO. (En lugar de 'I think he will be angry'). 
- Usar 'not' o 'not... so': 
A: Is the company going bankrupt? 
B: I hope NOT. / I don't think SO.
parts.audio: Substitution means using short words instead of repeating long ideas. A common substitution is using 'so'. If someone asks 'Will the CEO be angry?', you can reply: I think so. Or: I hope so. This replaces the whole phrase 'I think he will be angry'. For negative responses, use 'not' or 'not... so'. For example: Is the company going bankrupt? You can answer: I hope not. Or: I don't think so.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la forma más natural y eficiente (omitiendo o sustituyendo palabras).

questions.question:
A: Are we going to get a bonus this year? 
B: I hope ____. (Espero que sí).
questions.explanation: Con verbos como hope, think, suppose, se usa 'so' para sustituir una idea completa afirmativa.

questions.question:
A: Is the meeting cancelled? 
B: I don't think ____. (Creo que no).
questions.explanation: Con 'think' en negativo: I don't think so.

questions.question:
A: Will there be massive layoffs? 
B: I hope ____. (Espero que no).
questions.explanation: Con 'hope' en negativo: I hope not. (No se dice 'I don't hope so').

questions.question: I would love to help you with the project, but I simply don't have time ____. (Para hacerlo).
questions.explanation: Ellipsis del verbo: 'time to (help you)' -> time to.

questions.question: They told me to rewrite the report, so I ____. (Así lo hice / Lo hice).
questions.explanation: Sustitución de acción pasada completa con auxiliar: so I did.

questions.question: I wanted to attend the conference, but my boss told me not ____. (Que no lo hiciera).
questions.explanation: Ellipsis del infinitivo: told me not to (attend).

questions.question:
A: Did the board approve the budget? 
B: I suppose ____. (Supongo que sí).

A: Are they going to close the factory? 
B: I am afraid ____. (Me temo que sí).

A: Do we have to work this weekend? 
B: I am afraid ____. (Me temo que no).
questions.explanation: Sustitución negativa: I am afraid not.

questions.question: Some clients agreed with the new prices; ____ complained. (Otros).
questions.explanation: Sustitución de nombre plural: others (others clients).

questions.question: I've never been to Tokyo, but my colleague ____. (Él sí ha estado).
questions.explanation: Ellipsis usando el auxiliar del Present Perfect: but my colleague has (been to Tokyo).

questions.question: If you need a pen, I can lend you ____. (Uno).
questions.explanation: Sustitución de sustantivo contable singular: one.

questions.question: She doesn't like working from home, and neither ____ I. (A mí tampoco).
questions.explanation: Sustitución/inversión con neither: neither do I.

questions.question: He said he would send the email by 5 PM, but he ____. (No lo hizo).
questions.explanation: Ellipsis con auxiliar: but he didn't (send it).

questions.question: You can leave early today if you want ____. (Si quieres hacerlo).
questions.explanation: Ellipsis del infinitivo: if you want to (leave early).

questions.question: I don't think we will reach our sales target, and John doesn't think ____ either. (Tampoco lo cree).

A: Is the CFO resigning? 
B: It seems ____. (Parece que sí).
questions.explanation: Sustitución con seem: It seems so.

questions.question: I haven't read the report yet, but I am going ____ tonight. (A hacerlo).
questions.explanation: Ellipsis de infinitivo: I am going to (read it).

questions.question: These laptops are old. We need to buy new ____. (Nuevas).
questions.explanation: Sustitución de sustantivo plural: ones (new laptops -> new ones).

questions.question: I would help you, but I really can't ____. (No puedo hacerlo).
questions.explanation: O solo 'can't'. Si usamos afford: 'afford to' (permitírmelo, en términos de tiempo/esfuerzo).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la palabra de sustitución u omisión (so, not, to, did, has, ones).

questions.question:
A: Will we get a bonus? 
B: I hope ____. (Espero que sí)

A: Will they fire us? 
B: I hope ____. (Espero que no)

A: Is the deal closed? 
B: I don't think ____. (Creo que no)
I'd love to go, but I don't have time ____. (Para hacerlo - preposición)
He told me not ____. (Que no lo hiciera - preposición)
I haven't finished, but Sarah ____. (Ella sí ha terminado - auxiliar)
He said he would call, but he ____. (No lo hizo - auxiliar en pasado)
These computers are broken. Let's buy new ____. (Nuevas - pronombre plural)

A: Do we have to pay extra? 
B: I am afraid ____. (Me temo que sí)
If you need a cable, I can lend you ____. (Uno)

pairs.target: Él me dijo que no lo hiciera
